notes: Source: Neat's official "Neat Pad" device sheet (cdn-stories.neat.no PDF, © 2025 Neat) plus the matching product page at neat.no/pad/ — both manufacturer-authoritative and mutually consistent. This is the original 8-inch "Neat Pad" (touch controller for Zoom Rooms / Microsoft Teams Rooms on Android, doubling as a room-scheduling display), not the newer "Neat Pad Pro" variant Neat has since introduced (separate product with its own manual, not covered here). Physical I/O per the spec is limited to three items under "Networking & ports": Ethernet (PoE), USB-C (reserved/inactive), and an optional AC power adapter — WiFi is also listed there but is wireless, not a physical port, so it is omitted. No connector diagram/photo of the ports was found in any manufacturer document, so the AC-adapter connector type (set to dc-barrel) is an educated inference rather than a confirmed spec — hence "medium" confidence rather than "high." Ethernet link speed is likewise never stated, so no eth-* grade was applied. Dimensions: 7.8 x 1.7 x 5.0 in (198 x 42 x 127 mm), 1.15 lb (520 g); ships with wall mount and side mount; not rack-mountable (desktop/wall unit, so rackUnits omitted).

ports.name: Ethernet (PoE)
ports.note: Primary data + power connection. Supports Power over Ethernet: 802.3af PoE (Class 0 / mode A), 56V DC, 0.275A. Ethernet link speed (10/100/1000) is not stated by the manufacturer, so no bandwidth grade is set.

ports.name: USB-C
ports.note: Listed by Neat as "reserved for future use" — physically present but not functional in current firmware. No speed/version stated.

ports.name: Power adapter (AC, optional)
ports.note: Neat's spec sheet lists only "Power adapter for AC (optional)" as an alternate to PoE power; the exact device-side connector is not pictured or specified in any manufacturer document found. DC barrel is the closest/most likely match and is an inference, not a confirmed spec.
